arxiv-1601-02354.title: Cospectral lifts of graphs
arxiv-1601-02354.creator: F. Ramezani Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science,K.N.Toosi University of Technology, Tehran, Iran,P.O. Box 16315-1618 1[.3cm]
arxiv-1601-02354.description: Abstract We prove that for a pair of cospectral graphs G G and H H , there exist their non trivial lifts G ′ G^{\prime} and H ′ H^{\prime} which are cospectral. More over for a pair of cospectral graphs on 6 6 vertices, we find some cospectral lifts of them. AMS Subject Classification: 05C50.

arxiv-1806-00322.title: Direct optimisation of the discovery significance when training neural networks to search for new physics in particle colliders
arxiv-1806-00322.creator: and Dirk Krücker
arxiv-1806-00322.description: Abstract We introduce two new loss functions designed to directly optimise the statistical significance of the expected number of signal events when training neural networks to classify events as signal or background in the scenario of a search for new physics at a particle collider.

arxiv-2105-03016.title: Low Temperature Domain Wall Freezing and Non-Equilibrium Dynamics in the Transverse-Field Ising Model Material CoNb 2 O 6
arxiv-2105-03016.creator: C. L. Sarkis, S. Säubert, V. Williams, E.S. Choi, T. R. Reeder, H. S. Nair, K. A. Ross
arxiv-2105-03016.description: Abstract CoNb 2 O 6 is a rare realization of the transverse field Ising model (TFIM), making it a useful tool for studying both equilibrium and non-equilibrium many-body quantum physics. Despite a large body of work dedicated to characterizing this material, details of the ordered states in the presence of relatively weak transverse fields have not been discussed in detail.

arxiv-2210-14552.title: A Robust Bias Mitigation Procedure Based on the Stereotype Content Model
arxiv-2210-14552.creator: Eddie L. Ungless, Amy Rafferty, Hrichika Nag, Björn Ross
arxiv-2210-14552.description: Abstract The Stereotype Content model (SCM) states that we tend to perceive minority groups as cold, incompetent or both. In this paper we adapt existing work to demonstrate that the Stereotype Content model holds for contextualised word embeddings, then use these results to evaluate a fine-tuning process designed to drive a language model away from stereotyped portrayals of minority groups.

arxiv-2304-09448.title: EC 2 : {}^{2}: Emergent Communication for Embodied Control
arxiv-2304-09448.description: Abstract Embodied control requires agents to leverage multi-modal pre-training to quickly learn how to act in new environments, where video demonstrations contain visual and motion details needed for low-level perception and control, and language instructions support generalization with abstract, symbolic structures.

arxiv-2408-04651.title: Knowledge AI: Fine-tuning NLP Models for Facilitating Scientific Knowledge Extraction and Understanding
arxiv-2408-04651.creator: Hayden Beadles†, Kalyan Sashank Mupparaju†, Balaji Muralidharan†, Mahmoodreza Marzban†
arxiv-2408-04651.description: Abstract This project investigates the efficacy of Large Language Models (LLMs) in understanding and extracting scientific knowledge across specific domains and to create a deep learning framework: Knowledge AI. As a part of this framework, we employ pre-trained models and fine-tune them on datasets in the scientific domain.

arxiv-2411-00086.title: The Lyman Alpha Reference Sample
arxiv-2411-00086.creator: Le Reste A, Hayes M. J, Cannon J. M, Melinder J, Runnholm A, Rivera-Thorsen T. E, Östlin G, Adamo A, Herenz E. C, Schaerer D, Scarlata C, Kunth D

arxiv-2504-21798.creator: John Yang 1, Kilian Lieret 2, Carlos E. Jimenez 2, Alexander Wettig 2, Kabir Khandpur 3, Yanzhe Zhang 1, Binyuan Hui 4, Ofir Press 2, Ludwig Schmidt 1, Diyi Yang 1, 1 Stanford University, 2 Princeton University, 3 Indepedent, 4 Alibaba Qwen

Jimenez 2, Alexander Wettig 2, Kabir Khandpur 3, Yanzhe Zhang 1, Binyuan Hui 4, Ofir Press 2, Ludwig Schmidt 1, Diyi Yang 1, 1 Stanford University, 2 Princeton University, 3 Indepedent, 4 Alibaba Qwen. arxiv-2509-05898.title: Attention, Action, and Memory: How Multi-modal Interfaces and Cognitive Load Alter Information Retention DOI: TBD Conference: Proceedings of the 27th ACM International Conference on Multimodal Interaction; October 13–17, 2025; Canberra, Australia Proceedings of the 27th ACM International Conference
arxiv-2509-05898.creator: Omar Elgohary, Zhu-Tian Chen
arxiv-2509-05898.description: Abstract . Each year, multi-modal interaction continues to grow within both industry and academia. However, researchers have yet to fully explore the impact of multi-modal systems on learning and memory retention. This research investigates how combining gaze-based controls with gesture navigation affects information retention when compared to standard track-pad usage.

arxiv-2510-01074.title: \titlesize A TWO-LEVEL ENSEMBLE APPROACH FOR DIABETIC RETINOPATHY PREDICTION
arxiv-2510-01074.creator: Mahyar Mahmoudi 1, Tieming Liu 1 1 Oklahoma State University, Stillwater, OK, USA
arxiv-2510-01074.description: Abstract Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of blindness in the working-age population. Current diagnostic methods for DR, comprehensive ophthalmic exams, are constrained by the availability of ophthalmologists and special equipment. Retinal-image-based AI tools for DR screening are not effective in detecting DR in early stages.

arxiv-2601-16798.title: Superhumps in active dwarf novae.
arxiv-2601-16798.creator: Part I: ER Ursae Majoris
arxiv-2601-16798.description: Abstract We report photometry results of a frequently outbursting dwarf nova, ER Ursae Majoris. To measure the outburst parameters of the system, we carried out analyses of the light curve, periodograms, and O − C O-C diagrams. We investigated the system’s behaviour using the ground-based optical data and the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite data.

pmc-10693921.title: Bridging the Gap: Parents’ Knowledge of Childhood Developmental Milestones and the Early Identification of Children With Developmental Delay
pmc-10693921.creator: Haitham M Alghamdi, Bsaim A Altirkistani, Rabea A Baatya, Yasir O Marghalani, Nahla M Alshaikh
pmc-10693921.description: BackgroundMonitoring children's acquisition of developmental milestones is integral to pediatric practice. Though pediatricians are responsible for evaluating children’s development, parents have a crucial role in addressing delays as early as possible, where early detection of developmental delay can help in early intervention and ultimately potentiate a child’s cognitive and social abilities toward an independent life.

pmc-10743444.title: The Effect of Mice Adaptation Process on the Pathogenicity of Influenza A/South Africa/3626/2013 (H1N1)pdm09 Model Strain
pmc-10743444.creator: Mohammad Al Farroukh, Irina Kiseleva, Ekaterina Stepanova, Ekaterina Bazhenova, Elena Krutikova, Artem Tkachev, Anna Chistyakova, Andrey Rekstin, Ludmila Puchkova, Larisa Rudenko, James K Bashkin
pmc-10743444.description: Influenza virus strain A/South Africa/3626/2013 (H1N1)pdm09 (SA-WT) is a non-mouse-adapted model strain that has naturally high pathogenic properties in mice. It has been suggested that the high pathogenicity of this strain for mice could be due to the three strain-specific substitutions in the polymerase complex (Q687R in PB1, N102T in PB2, and E358E/K heterogeneity in PB2).

pmc-11490075.title: Calculating the Expected Net Benefit of Sampling for Survival Data: A Tutorial and Case Study
pmc-11490075.creator: Mathyn Vervaart
pmc-11490075.description: The net value of reducing decision uncertainty through collecting additional data is quantified by the expected net benefit of sampling (ENBS). The ENBS is the difference between the population-level expected value of sample information (EVSI) for the data collection exercise and the costs associated with the data collection.

pmc-12497752.title: Comparative chloroplast genomes and phylogenetic analysis of six Periploca species from China provide insights into the distinction of members of this small medicinal genus
pmc-12497752.creator: Tian Shuai, Qianli Li, Jinlan Long, Xiaoqi Jiang, Linling Wei, Ning Ding, Wei Zhou, Zhikun Wu
pmc-12497752.description: IntroductionThe genus Periploca L. (Apocynaceae) comprises approximately 17 species worldwide and possesses considerable medicinal value. However, owing to morphological similarities in vegetative organs, specimens and living plants usually lacking flowers and fruits are difficult to determine to species level posing challenges for its proper medicinal utilization.

pmc-12566940.title: Thermal Stability and Decomposition Mechanisms of PVA/PEGDA–PEGMA IPN-Hydrogels: A Multimethod Kinetic Approach
pmc-12566940.creator: Akmaral Zh Sarsenbekova, Ulygbek B Tuleuov, Akerke T Kazhmuratova, Abylaikhan N Bolatbay, Lyazzat Zh Zhaparova, Yerkeblan M Tazhbayev, Fei Han
pmc-12566940.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the thermal stability and decomposition mechanisms of IPN hydrogels based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and a copolymer network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate–poly(ethylene glycol) methacrylate (PEGDA–PEGMA). Using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA/DTG) and multi-approach kinetic analysis (Friedman and Ozawa–Flynn–Wall isoconversion methods, nonparametric kinetics, Shestaka-Berggren model), the influence of composition on the processes of dehydration, thermal destruction, and the distribution of activation energy by degrees of conversion was investigated.

pmc-12719896.title: Energy2MOB study, group food education programme to reduce obesity in adults: randomised clinical trial protocol
pmc-12719896.creator: Mar Gargallo-Civil, Anna Ruiz-Comellas, Laia Sola, Cristina Vaque-Crusellas
pmc-12719896.description: IntroductionObesity is a prevalent multifactorial disease worldwide that has become a major public health concern. Excess adiposity poses a health risk because it is related to several chronic diseases, which impact the person’s quality of life and present a greater risk of mortality.

pmc-13209406.title: Optical Biosensors—Principles of Operation and Applications
pmc-13209406.creator: Tomasz Blachowicz, Guido Ehrmann, Elzbieta Stepula, Andrea Ehrmann
pmc-13209406.description: Biosensors have a recognition element that detects a bioanalyte as well as a transducer that transfers the measured physicochemical properties into an electric signal, which is amplified, processed, and depicted on a user interface and usually stored in a data storage system.

pmc-13382457.title: Clinical outcomes of invasive versus conservative strategies for very high-risk patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: an observational cohort study in a real-world population of China
pmc-13382457.creator: Yuanhui Liu, Lin Zeng, ShiJie Yu, Xuhui Lin, Kailun Qiu, Peng Yin, Chongyang Duan, Ling Xue, Maigeng Zhou, Feng Liu, Ning Tan, Pengcheng He
pmc-13382457.description: SummaryBackgroundAlthough an invasive strategy (IS) within 2 h is recommended for very high-risk patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS), the optimal strategies remained debated due to a lack of evidence, because these patients were excluded from clinical studies.

pmc-13447015.title: An injectable self-healing curcumin-sustained-release hydrogel for lower limb ischemia via autophagy inhibition by Atp6v0d2 downregulation
pmc-13447015.creator: Hanfei Tang, Fang Wang, Tonglei Han, Xuanyong Liu, Minhui Li, Jiaqi Zhu, Xiao Tang, Guowei Liu, Jiajun Qiu, Daqiao Guo
pmc-13447015.description: Although hydrophobic drugs demonstrate the promising therapeutic efficacy for peripheral artery disease in vitro, their in vivo performance is often hindered by low bioavailability due to inherent hydrophobicity. To address this, an injectable, self-healing and curcumin-sustained-release hydrogel (CGP hydrogel) using a gelatin/polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel (GP hydrogel) was developed.

pmc-13507706.title: Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis With Multifocal Pancreatic and Renal Pseudotumors, Mimicking Neoplasm: A Case Report
pmc-13507706.creator: Surbhi Singh, Akhil Tanwar, Dhrumil Patel, Jonathan Von Reusner, Prabath Kumar Mondel, Ashlesha Udare
pmc-13507706.description: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) is an ANCA‐associated small‐vessel vasculitis that can rarely present as a mass‐like inflammatory pseudotumor in the abdomen. We report a 52‐year‐old woman with systemic symptoms and laboratory evidence of GPA with multiple heterogeneous mass lesions involving the pancreas and both kidneys on CT imaging. These lesions mimicked a neoplasm, prompting further characterization with tissue sampling.

pmc-13520396.title: Primary left atrial spindle cell sarcoma with low-grade malignant features mimicking recurrent myxoma: a case report
pmc-13520396.creator: Jing-wei Zhang, Yi Wang, Wei Li, Feng-juan Yao, Dong-hong Liu

pmc-13538362.title: Inhibition of ERK5 activity ameliorates osteoarthritis by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated chondrocyte pyroptosis
pmc-13538362.creator: Baolin Zhang, Peihang Fang, Jiahui Long, Deying Su, Hengyu Liu, Ricong Weng, Gengjia Chen, Yingtong Chen, GuanHong Chen, Zhiheng Liao, Taifeng Zhou, Shuqing Chen, Peiqiang Su, Caixia Xu
pmc-13538362.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Osteoarthritis (OA) is a widespread degenerative joint disorder manifesting as chronic pain, functional impairment, and progressive disability, imposing a substantial burden on global public health. Despite extensive research, the precise molecular pathways underlying OA pathogenesis remain incompletely elucidated. Our data indicated that human OA cartilage and cartilaginous tissues from aged mice exhibited markedly elevated levels of extracellular signal-related kinase 5 (ERK5) enzyme activity.

pmc-13687570.title: Viral Infection‐Induced Epilepsy and the Gut Microbiome Crosstalk
pmc-13687570.creator: Xi Guo, Niomi R Kaiser, Susan L Campbell
pmc-13687570.description: Viral infections of the central nervous system (CNS) pose a significant risk for seizures, and in some cases, long‐term epileptogenesis. Seizure development following viral infection involves diverse CNS mechanisms, with emerging evidence that peripheral factors, including gut microbiome composition and immune‐inflammatory responses, also contribute.
